overview: S&P Global is a leading provider of credit ratings, financial data, benchmarks, and analytics serving global capital, commodity, and automotive markets. Following the July 1, 2026 spin-off of its Mobility division (now independent Mobility Global Inc., ticker MBGL), the company operates through four segments: Ratings, Market Intelligence, Energy (formerly Commodity Insights, now including supply-chain assets), and S&P Dow Jones Indices. Its benchmark franchises in Ratings, Indices, and Platts energy pricing collectively generate roughly 65% of revenue and 80% of operating profit, reflecting a business built around indispensable, recurring, high-margin information infrastructure for global finance and energy markets.

business_model.summary: S&P Global monetizes proprietary benchmarks, data, and ratings through a mix of transaction-linked fees (bond issuance ratings), subscriptions (data/analytics terminals, Platts price assessments), and asset-based/royalty fees (index licensing on ETFs and AUM-linked products like the S&P 500). Ratings revenue is tied to debt issuance volumes and is partly cyclical; Indices and Market Intelligence are largely recurring subscription or AUM-linked revenue; Energy (Commodity Insights) sells subscription price benchmarks and analytics to energy/commodity traders. Post-Mobility spin-off, the company is a purer play on capital markets infrastructure and benchmarks.
business_model.customer_type: B2B — institutional investors, investment banks, corporate issuers, asset managers, commodity traders, and index licensees (ETF sponsors); essentially no direct consumer exposure post-Mobility spin-off
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily US/Americas with significant EMEA and growing Asia-Pacific presence; ratings and indices activity skews toward US and European capital markets while Energy has meaningful exposure to global commodity hubs

competitive_position.market_position: S&P Global and Moody's form a duopoly controlling roughly 80% of the global credit ratings market (S&P ~50%, Moody's ~31%, Fitch ~12%, others ~7%); S&P Dow Jones Indices is the benchmark provider for the S&P 500 and numerous widely-licensed indices; Platts is the dominant price-reporting agency in oil, gas, and petrochemicals

moat_factors.description: NRSRO designation and decades of regulatory/market embedding make new ratings entrants nearly impossible; most bond covenants and regulations require ratings from recognized agencies
150+ year history; S&P and Moody's ratings are the default reference standard baked into regulations, covenants, and investment mandates
Index licenses (S&P 500) and Market Intelligence/Capital IQ workflows are deeply embedded in client processes, trillions in AUM benchmarked to S&P indices
More liquidity and AUM tracking an index reinforces its status as the benchmark, attracting further licensing
Decades of proprietary pricing data (Platts) and financial data create a scale advantage difficult to replicate, though AI tools lower some data-aggregation barriers

weaknesses: Ratings revenue is cyclical and tied to debt capital markets issuance volumes, creating earnings volatility in rate-shock or credit-stress periods
Market Intelligence desktop/data products face rising competitive and pricing pressure from AI-enabled research tools and lower-cost alternatives
Reliance on continued regulatory recognition (NRSRO status) — a structural but not unassailable moat
Integration complexity remains post-IHS Markit merger and now post-Mobility spin-off, with two major corporate reorganizations in recent years

growth_drivers: Private credit ratings — a fast-growing niche (Ratings segment private markets revenue grew ~25% YoY in recent quarters) as the private credit market has scaled to ~$3.5 trillion
AI/hyperscaler-driven technology debt issuance — record tech-sector bond issuance tied to ~$600B of 2026 hyperscaler capex supporting data center buildouts
S&P Dow Jones Indices — fastest-growing segment (revenue +20% in Q2 2026), benefiting from passive investing growth, new thematic/private-markets indices, and AUM-linked royalties
Enterprise AI initiatives ("Spark Assist" and other GenAI tools) embedding AI into workflow products to defend and expand Market Intelligence share
Expansion into private markets data/benchmarks (private credit indices, private equity data) as a new high-growth adjacency
Leveraged loan refinancing wall (2027-2028 maturities) expected to drive future issuance and ratings activity
Capital return — increased 2026 buyback target to over $7 billion plus a 52-year dividend growth streak (Dividend Aristocrat)
Simplified, more focused portfolio post-Mobility spin-off sharpening capital allocation toward core data/ratings/benchmark franchises

business.description: Ratings revenue (largest segment) is highly sensitive to bond and loan issuance volumes, which can swing sharply with rate changes or credit market stress
Off-the-shelf AI/LLM tools could erode demand for some Market Intelligence desktop research products, though risk is concentrated in a minority of revenue (estimated under ~6-10%)

business.risk: Customer concentration in capital markets intermediaries
business.description: Large banks and asset managers represent significant revenue blocks in Market Intelligence and Indices

business.risk: Execution risk from recent corporate reorganizations
business.description: Completed Mobility spin-off (July 2026) and prior IHS Markit integration add management complexity and could create cost dis-synergies

financial.description: Total debt rose to ~$16.0B (Q1 2026) partly reflecting balance sheet actions around the Mobility separation; net debt/EBITDA around 1.4-1.8x is manageable but up from historical lows
International revenue (EMEA, APAC) creates translation exposure, though business is majority USD-denominated

regulatory.description: SEC and international regulators oversee ratings agency conduct, conflicts of interest (issuer-pays model), and fee structures; any adverse rule change could affect Ratings economics

regulatory.risk: Antitrust/market structure scrutiny of index/ratings duopoly
regulatory.description: Periodic regulatory and academic scrutiny of the ratings oligopoly and potential conflicts in the issuer-pays model, though no imminent structural remedy is pending

regulatory.risk: Data privacy and cross-border data regulation
regulatory.description: Increasing data localization/privacy rules (EU, China) could raise compliance costs for global data operations

macro.description: Higher-for-longer rates suppress bond issuance and refinancing activity, directly hitting Ratings revenue; lower rates typically boost issuance
Indices segment revenue is partly AUM/asset-value linked, so a sustained equity market selloff would reduce royalty revenue
A recession could simultaneously reduce new issuance (Ratings) and increase downgrade/default-related volatility, with mixed but net-negative effects
Energy/Commodity Insights subscription revenue is relatively resilient but new product/market activity can slow in extended low-volatility commodity markets

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global ratings and financial data market is expected to grow mid-to-high single digits, supported by record corporate debt issuance (especially tech/AI-related), private credit market expansion (~$3.5T and growing), and continued index/ETF asset growth; company guiding to 6-8% organic constant-currency revenue growth for 2026
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high in Ratings (tied to capital markets issuance cycles); low in Indices and Market Intelligence (largely recurring/subscription and AUM-linked revenue provides ballast)
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — rate levels and rate-change expectations are a primary driver of bond/loan issuance volumes and thus Ratings segment revenue
key_input_costs: Technology/cloud infrastructure and AI compute costs

recent_developments.event: Completed spin-off of Mobility division as independent public company Mobility Global Inc. (NYSE: MBGL); shareholders received 1 MBGL share per SPGI share held as of June 15, 2026 record date
Reported pro forma (ex-Mobility) revenue of $3.678B, up 11% YoY; adjusted EPS of $4.83, up 23% YoY; adjusted operating margin expanded 200bps to 54.3%; Ratings revenue +17%, Indices +20%
Private markets/private credit ratings revenue grew approximately 25% YoY, highlighted by management and analysts as a key emerging growth driver ahead of the Mobility separation
Raised full-year 2026 share repurchase target to over $7 billion (from prior guidance), with $1.5B executed year-to-date as of Q2 2026 report
Board approved dividend increase to $0.97/share quarterly, extending the company's 52-year consecutive dividend growth streak (Dividend Aristocrat)

Hosted Investor Day unveiling medium-term targets: 7-9% organic constant-currency revenue growth, 50-75bps annual adjusted operating margin expansion, and double-digit adjusted diluted EPS growth, alongside strategic pillars of market leadership, high-growth adjacencies (private markets), and enterprise AI
S&P Global Ratings published 2026 credit market outlook flagging private credit growth, AI/tech-driven issuance, and rising leverage as key themes shaping rating activity
Launched new private credit/private loan index benchmarks via S&P Dow Jones Indices, extending benchmark franchise into private markets

items.notes: GAAP revenue growth guided at 5.9%-7.9%, reflecting continuing operations post-Mobility spin-off
Raised following strong Q2 2026 beat (Q2 adjusted EPS +23% YoY)
Reflects debt issuance volumes and private credit ratings momentum
Strongest-growing segment, driven by AUM growth and new product launches
Subscription-based growth amid AI-related competitive pressure
Includes former Commodity Insights plus consolidated supply chain assets post-Mobility separation
Increased from prior target; $1.5B executed year-to-date as of Q2 2026
Introduced at November 2025 Investor Day alongside 50-75bps annual margin expansion and double-digit adjusted EPS growth targets

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Martina Cheung has emphasized three strategic pillars: advancing market leadership in core benchmark businesses, expanding into high-growth adjacencies (notably private markets/private credit), and amplifying enterprise capabilities through AI. Management highlighted private credit ratings revenue growth of ~25% YoY as validating the adjacency strategy, and framed the Mobility spin-off as sharpening focus on the core data/ratings/benchmark franchise. Commentary has stressed confidence in continued margin expansion and double-digit EPS growth even amid AI-driven competitive change in Market Intelligence.

bull_case: Ratings/Indices duopoly-to-oligopoly structure with regulatory barriers to entry provides durable pricing power and ~80%+ operating margins in benchmark businesses
Private credit ratings is a genuine new growth vector (~25% YoY growth) expanding the addressable market beyond traditional public bond issuance
S&P Dow Jones Indices is compounding fastest (+20% revenue in Q2 2026), levered to structural growth in passive investing and AUM
Post-Mobility spin-off, SPGI is a simpler, higher-margin, more focused pure-play on data/ratings/benchmarks with a cleaner growth and capital-return story
Shareholder-friendly capital returns — raised 2026 buyback target to over $7 billion plus a 52-year dividend growth streak — supported by high free cash flow conversion and asset-light economics
bear_case: Ratings revenue remains structurally tied to debt issuance cycles; a higher-for-longer rate environment or credit market stress would directly compress the largest and most profitable segment
AI-enabled research and data tools pose a genuine, if currently modest, long-term disintermediation risk to Market Intelligence desktop products and data subscriptions
Elevated leverage (~$16B total debt as of Q1 2026) following balance sheet actions around the Mobility spin-off reduces financial flexibility versus SPGI's historically pristine balance sheet

Premium valuation (forward P/E in the low-20s) leaves limited room for execution missteps, especially given two major corporate reorganizations (IHS Markit integration, Mobility spin-off) in recent years
Regulatory scrutiny of the issuer-pays ratings model and index-provider concentration is a persistent, low-probability but high-impact tail risk to the core moat
